name: arpeggio climb
origin: original, written in the idiom of Guns N' Roses
feel: arpeggiated triads sequenced up the neck
notes: Triad tones picked one to a beat, the shape moving up a position each bar.  Major pentatonic over a I-V-vi-IV loop.

name: downbeat stomp
origin: original, written in the idiom of KISS
notes: Pentatonic box one, root on the low E, every phrase landing on beat one.  I-bVII-IV, the flat-seventh move.

name: quiet loud
origin: original, written in the idiom of Nirvana
notes: Two-note shapes, no third, shifted by a tritone and a minor second.  Dynamics swing hard between verse and chorus.

name: twelve bar
idiom: the blues the other three came out of
origin: original, written in the idiom of the blues the other three came out of
notes: A twelve bar in E.  Public domain form, here so the corpus has one loop whose harmony moves slowly enough to hear the fly follow it.

name: gallop
origin: original, written in the idiom of Iron Maiden
feel: fast triplet gallop, high on the neck
notes: Minor runs taken quickly, the harmony climbing bVI-bVII back to the root.  Fastest thing in the corpus and the highest register.

name: slow burn
origin: original, written in the idiom of Black Sabbath
feel: half time, heavy, low and slow
notes: The slowest loop, sitting on the low strings.  Against the gallop it is unmistakably a different piece rather than the same one rephrased.

name: mixolydian strut
origin: original, written in the idiom of AC/DC
feel: open-string strut, major with a flat seven
notes: Major third and a flat seventh - the one loop here that is not minor, so it reads as bright next to everything else.
